query: Why do atoms form covalent bonds?
title: Why Atoms Form Covalent Bonds

scenes.title: The Drive for Electronic Stability
scenes.narration: Atoms in nature seek electronic stability, striving to achieve complete outer valence shells with eight electrons.
scenes.key_takeaway: Atoms seek complete outer valence shells to achieve stable configurations.

scenes.title: Orbital Overlap and Electron Sharing
scenes.narration: When nonmetal atoms encounter one another, their high electronegativity drives them to share valence electron pairs.
scenes.key_takeaway: Nonmetals share electron pairs rather than transferring them.

scenes.title: Electrostatic Molecular Binding
scenes.narration: These shared negative electrons attract both positive nuclei simultaneously, creating a strong electrostatic molecular bond.
scenes.key_takeaway: Simultaneous attraction of nuclei to shared electrons holds the bond tight.

scenes.title: The Architecture of Molecular Matter
scenes.narration: Through covalent sharing, essential molecules like water, methane, and DNA build the architecture of our world.
scenes.key_takeaway: Covalent bonds build discrete, robust molecular structures.
